newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits new high on dollar's strength.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits new high on dollar's strength.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange followed other bullish European markets on Tuesday and rallied to a new all-time high on the back of the dollar's strength, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 3,760.99 points, up 46.31. The previous high of 3,728.58 points was reached on October 17.
"It's evident that the dollar played the key role," said Istvan Simon of Concorde Securities.
"There was not any company news behind the rise and the Dow Jones also slipped a bit yesterday, so nothing else explains the rise."
While all shares closed higher or unchanged, the bourse suspended trading for the whole day in Csopak Rt and in Cofinec, after an initial surge, for the rest of the day.

An analyst said earlier today the possible reason behind Cofinec Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs)' surge was that Cofinec officials invited a group of analysts to visit their plants in Poland and Hungary. Cofinec confirmed the visit.
Cofinec GDRs opened at 4,060 forints, below Monday's close at 4,065 forints, and after they soared to 5,460 forints by 1135 GMT.

Trading in Csopak, which is involved in trading, as well as milling and cosmetics, was suspended following a newspaper report about a new Csopak acquisition the company has not yet reported because it had not yet been officially informed by Hungary's state privatisation agency APV.

However, Csopak informed the bourse ahead of trading that Chance 96 Kft, a company in which it has a 49 percent stake, has submitted a bid to APV to acquire 98 percent in trading company Pannonker Rt.
On Monday, Csopak shares closed at 1,190 forints.
Elsewhere on the market the beverage sector extended Monday's rise. Spirits maker Zwack rose 150 forints to 2,750, while brewery Sopron gained 145 forints to 2,665.
Chemicals Borsodchem hit a new high of 3,510 forints and closed there, up 110.
